page_metadata.title: Development, Testing, Parameterization, and Calibration of a Human Physiologically Based Pharmacokinetic Model for the Plasticizer, Hexamoll® Diisononyl-Cyclohexane-1, 2-Dicarboxylate Using In Silico, In Vitro, and Human Biomonitoring Data

model_classification.evidence_quote: A physiologically based pharmacokinetic model for Hexamoll® diisononyl-cyclohexane-1,2-dicarboxylate was developed to interpret the biokinetics in humans after single oral doses.

model_context.model_origin: new human PBPK model parameterized with in silico/in vitro data and calibrated with human biomonitoring data
model_context.stated_purpose: Interpret human biokinetics after a single oral dose of Hexamoll DINCH and simulate urinary metabolite excretion
model_context.dose_metric: urinary cx-MINCH and OH-MINCH concentrations; venous DINCH and MINCH concentrations

stated_assumptions.description: The model contains a lymphatic compartment because part of the oral dose bypasses the liver and enters venous blood via a lymph node.
stated_assumptions.evidence_quote: the presence of a lymphatic compartment was deemed an important component of model structure.

stated_assumptions.description: DINCH to MINCH biotransformation occurs in liver and gut; MINCH to OH-/cx-MINCH is ascribed to liver.
stated_assumptions.evidence_quote: The biotransformation of DINCH to MINCH occurs in both the liver and gut. In the MINCH sub-model the biotransformation of MINCH to cx- and OH-MINCH is ascribed only to the liver.

stated_assumptions.description: Volunteer C urinary data were judged unreliable and excluded from the final simultaneous calibration.
stated_assumptions.evidence_quote: Urinary data from participant C was judged to be unreliable.

connections.evidence: Fraction enters lymphatic system via lacteals
Urinary excretion of metabolites with bladder compartment

absorption.model_type: mechanistic gastric emptying + gut absorption + lymphatic uptake
absorption.evidence_quote: A portion of the oral dose entered the hepatic portal vein and another portion into the lymphatic system via lacteals.

metabolism.evidence_quote: DINCH is biotransformed to MINCH in liver and gut; MINCH is further biotransformed to OH-MINCH and cx-MINCH in liver.

elimination.evidence_quote: Urinary excretion of metabolites was described with first-order elimination rate constants and a bladder compartment.
